findings.description: Re-verify ledger [31]: FIXED. run_states now marks only the newest unfinished run in_progress; older unfinished runs are classified as interrupted.
Re-verify ledger [32]: FIXED. merge_pr wraps the temporary clone in try/finally with shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True), so a failed merge no longer leaks the clone.
Re-verify ledger [36]: FIXED. test_acceptance_broken_skill hard-asserts analyze.is_file() before loading the analyzer, so a relocated script fails loudly instead of skipping.

Re-verify ledger [33]/[54]: STILL PRESENT. finish() writes vendors=list(cfg.vendors) into the RunRecord, not the effective vendor list computed by effective_vendors(). A configured vendor that no scenario declares is recorded as having run.
findings.resolution: Capture the effective vendor list in _locked_run and pass it to finish(); default to cfg.vendors only on the pre-load guard paths.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [37]/[57]: STILL PRESENT. install_gh_shim writes a shebang of f"#!{sys.executable}" so the shim is bound to the interpreter of the process that materialized it. If the nightly runs under a venv that is later moved or removed, every gh call in retained workspaces fails with ENOENT.
findings.resolution: Use #!/usr/bin/env python3 or document the interpreter binding in the design, since workspaces are per-run and short-lived.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [42]/[58]: STILL PRESENT. NightlyConfig declares a judge: JudgeCfg field but run_nightly never reads cfg.judge; the judge_backend passed to run_scenario is always the function parameter (None from the CLI). The config knob is accepted by the schema and silently ignored.
findings.resolution: Either construct the judge backend from cfg.judge when judge_backend is None, or drop the field from the config model and schema until the judge is wired.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [43]: STILL PRESENT. `gaps flush` has --spool, --url-env and --key-env but no --config, so an operator cannot point it at the spool_path the nightly config resolves; they must re-derive the XDG path by hand.
findings.existing_code: flush.add_argument("--spool", type=Path, default=None, help="spool JSONL (default: XDG state)")
findings.resolution: Add --config that loads NightlyConfig and uses cfg.spool_path() and cfg.gaps env names when --spool is not given.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [46]: STILL PRESENT. _post_memory_query catches URLError, OSError and json.JSONDecodeError but not UnicodeDecodeError or a generic ValueError from a non-UTF-8 or non-object body; the SKILL.md claim that the analysis 'falls back gracefully with a warning if a query fails' is not satisfied on that path.
findings.resolution: Catch ValueError (which covers JSONDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError) alongside URLError/OSError.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [59]: STILL PRESENT. resolve_agent_id returns the IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID value verbatim, so build_memory_query(agent_id=None) with a comma-separated env value sends agent_id='a,b' as a single id. query_memory is correct because it uses resolve_agent_ids, but the public build_memory_query helper (tested by test_improve_harness.py) still produces an invalid request for the documented comma-separated form.
findings.resolution: Have build_memory_query take the first id from resolve_agent_ids(agent_id), or document that it is single-agent only.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [38]: STILL PRESENT. skills_sha runs `git status --porcelain` over the whole checkout, so any unrelated dirty file (for example a results file under the repo) marks skills_sha as +dirty even when skills/ is clean.
findings.resolution: Scope the status call: git status --porcelain -- <skills_root>.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [44]: STILL PRESENT. skills/tests/improve-harness/fixtures/capability-gap-entry.example.json is a hand copy of the package's example payload with no test asserting equality against packages/agent-scenarios' copy, so the two can drift silently.
findings.resolution: Add a test that loads both files and asserts the JSON objects are equal, or make one file the single source and resolve it relative to the repo root.

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [47]: STILL PRESENT. In the 'how the sources complement each other' bullet list of memory-conventions.md, a blank line separates the scenario-parity bullet from the four preceding bullets, rendering it as a separate list.

Re-verify ledger [45]: STILL PRESENT. The module docstring of test_memory_tag_conventions.py still says the source tag prefix 'works for all four vocabulary values' although SOURCE_VOCABULARY now lists five entries including scenario-parity.
findings.existing_code: - source: tag prefix works for all four vocabulary values

findings.description: Re-verify ledger [35]: FIXED. SKILL.md Prerequisites now document COORDINATION_API_KEY as a Bearer token, the per-agent_id query with both default ids, and the --agent-id / IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID override; analyze_failures.py accepts --agent-id as described.

Retention bound is off by one against the stated acceptance criterion. _prune_run_dirs runs before run_dir.mkdir, so after a run the workspaces directory holds retain_failed_runs + 1 directories (the test keeps 3 old dirs plus the new run). proposal.md's acceptance table says kept workspaces are '≤ retain_failed_runs run directories'. The spec scenario ('at the start of the next run ... older than the newest retain_failed_runs SHALL be deleted') matches the code, so this is a proposal/code wording mismatch rather than a behavior bug.
findings.existing_code:
_prune_run_dirs(workspaces, cfg.retain_failed_runs)
    run_dir = workspaces / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
findings.resolution: Either prune with keep=retain_failed_runs - 1 before creating the run dir, or reword the proposal acceptance row to 'retain_failed_runs previous run directories plus the current run'.

findings.description: flush_spool is a module-level function that calls the private SpoolMemorySink._flushing() and _read_lines() members, splitting the spool's locking protocol between the class and a free function. A later change to the class internals breaks the replay path without a type or import error.
findings.existing_code:
with spool._flushing():
        with spool.locked():
            snapshot = spool._read_lines()
findings.resolution: Move the replay into a SpoolMemorySink.flush(coordinator) method and keep flush_spool as a thin wrapper, or make the two helpers public.

findings.description: test_acceptance_broken_skill.py mixes absolute (`from tests.test_nightly_config import write_config`, `from tests.test_seed_outcomes import outcome_module`) and relative (`from .conftest import SCENARIOS_DIR`) imports of sibling test modules. The absolute form only resolves because pytest's rootdir puts packages/agent-scenarios on sys.path; running the file from another cwd or under a different importmode fails on one form but not the other.
findings.existing_code:
from tests.test_nightly_config import write_config
from tests.test_seed_outcomes import outcome_module

from .conftest import SCENARIOS_DIR
findings.resolution: Use relative imports for all three, matching test_seed_suite.py and test_seed_outcomes.py.

findings.description: test_default_executor_factory_wires_hermetic_settings asserts on CLIVendorExecutor private attributes (_timeout, _env_scrub, _env_set, _always_scrub, _skills_root). The test pins the executor's internal field names rather than its behavior, so a harmless rename breaks it while a wiring regression that keeps the names passes.
findings.existing_code: assert ex._timeout == 77 and ex._env_scrub == ("EXTRA",) and ex._env_set == {"FOO": "bar"}
findings.resolution: Acceptable for a wiring test; optionally expose a read-only settings view on CLIVendorExecutor and assert on it.

findings.description: SKILL.md's Data Sources table says frequency for scenario-parity 'counts (run, vendor) pairs, not nights', and SKILL.md's dedup rule says dedup is keyed on (capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id). Since the gap emitter sets session_id to the run_id and the same run emits one entry per vendor, the two statements are only consistent because dedup happens after per-source normalization with vendor preserved; the SKILL text does not say that, so a reader will expect vendor duplicates within a run to collapse to one. The acceptance test confirms frequency 2 for two vendors in one run, so behavior is correct; the documentation of the dedup key is incomplete.
findings.existing_code: Deduplication is keyed on `(capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id)`. When the same gap appears from multiple sources, all sources are preserved — cross-source agreement is the strongest signal.
findings.resolution: Note that scenario-parity entries are additionally distinguished by vendor (vendor:<id> tag), so two vendors failing in one run count twice.
